note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a FJI 11; A06b FJI 11; L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. On 2026-11-03 the primaries were read: the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' page (five of ten years; no renunciation, s. 11(2) of the Citizenship of Fiji Act 2009); Parliament's Bill No. 8 of 2026 (8 of 10 years) and Bill No. 16 of 2022 (15 of 20); the Ministry of Immigration's page, which says every child born in Fiji is a citizen unless a parent has diplomatic immunity and neither parent is a citizen. The Act itself couldn't be read at first, so birth in the territory was held to the dataset's reading, none, and the entry stayed at second hand. The same day the Act was read on laws.gov.fj (the Office of the Solicitor-General's consolidation, last updated 10 August 2026), with the 2013 Constitution, s. 5, and Act No. 10 of 2026. Every figure the file holds now rests on them, and the dataset is no longer cited. The Act reversed that hold, made only because the Act hadn't been read: every child born in Fiji is a citizen at birth unless a parent has diplomatic immunity and neither parent is a citizen (s. 6), so birth in the territory is unconditional (the diplomat exception isn't held by the form). A child born abroad to a citizen parent becomes a citizen by registration, not at birth (s. 8), now held as the limit abroad. A citizen keeps it on taking another (Constitution s. 5(4)(a)); holding another citizenship doesn't restrict naturalisation (s. 14). Act No. 10 of 2026 (passed 28 May 2026) will make the years 8 of 10 from a commencement the Minister appoints by notice in the Gazette (s. 1(2)); no such notice was found among 2026's published legal notices, so the 5 years stand.

sources.title: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Fiji (Fiji High Commission, Wellington), Fiji Citizenship
sources.said: Citizenship by registration covers six categories of individuals. The first category covers children born outside the Fiji Islands on or after 10th April 2009 if at the date of the child’s birth, either of the Child’s parents was a citizen – section 8(1) of the Citizenship of Fiji Act 2009. ... A foreign national can apply for Fiji citizenship if he or she has been lawfully present in Fiji for a total of five (5) of the ten (10) years immediately before the application is made. With the introduction of the multiple citizenship policy applicants do NOT need to renounce their other citizenship – Section 11 (2) of the Citizenship of Fiji Act 2009. Dual Citizenship The Fiji Government recognizes the existence of dual nationality ...

sources.title: Ministry of Immigration, Fiji, Citizenship By Birth
sources.said: The process of citizenship acquisition is guided by Fijian Citizenship Act 2009 that came into force on 10 April 2009. ... Every child born in Fiji on or after the commencement date becomes a citizen at the date of birth unless, at the date of birth: A parent of the child has the diplomatic immunity accorded to envoys of sovereign foreign power accredited to Fiji; and Neither parent is a citizen.

sources.said: (a) has been lawfully present in Fiji for a total of 8 of the 10 years immediately before the application for naturalisation; ... the Bill also streamlines the Act ... while repealing two uncommenced amendment Acts to consolidate the legal framework. ... From the commencement of the Citizenship of Fiji (Amendment) Act 2026 until 1 January 2035, a person qualifies for naturalisation if they have lawfully lived in Fiji for a total of eight years within the ten years immediately before applying ...

sources.title: Parliament of the Republic of Fiji, Bill No. 16 of 2022, Citizenship of Fiji (Revised Budget Amendment) Bill 2022, explanatory note
sources.said: Currently, a person only needs to be lawfully present in Fiji for 5 out of the 10 years prior to lodging an application for citizenship by naturalisation. The Bill seeks to increase the requisite aggregate period prior to lodgement from 5 out of 10 years to 15 out of 20 years.

sources.title: Citizenship of Fiji Act 2009, s. 6 Citizenship by birth (Laws of Fiji consolidated, Office of the Solicitor-General, laws.gov.fj; act last updated 10 August 2026)
sources.said: Citizenship by birth Every child born in Fiji on or after the commencement date becomes a citizen at the date of birth unless, at the date of birth— (a) a parent of the child has the diplomatic immunity accorded to envoys of sovereign foreign powers accredited to Fiji; and (b) neither parent is a citizen.

sources.title: Citizenship of Fiji Act 2009, s. 8 Who may apply for registration (laws.gov.fj consolidated)
sources.said: (1) A child born outside Fiji may become a citizen by registration on or after the commencement date if, at the time of the child's birth, either parent was a citizen. ... (5) An application for registration under subsection (1) , (2) or (3) made by the child concerned after he or she has reached the age of 18 must not be granted unless he or she has been lawfully present in Fiji for a total of 3 of the 5 years immediately before the application.

sources.title: Citizenship of Fiji Act 2009, s. 11 Availability of citizenship by naturalisation (laws.gov.fj consolidated, act last updated 10 August 2026)
sources.said: (2) In order to qualify for the grant of a certificate of naturalisation under section 13 a person must have been lawfully present in Fiji for a total of 5 of the 10 years immediately before the application for naturalisation is made.

sources.title: Citizenship of Fiji Act 2009, s. 14 Effect of possession of another citizenship on application for citizenship (laws.gov.fj consolidated)
sources.said: A person who possesses or has acquired the citizenship of one or more other countries is not restricted in applying for and being granted citizenship either by registration or by naturalisation solely by virtue of possessing or having acquired the citizenship of one or more other countries.

atBirth.descentAbroad: Person is born outside Fiji to a parent who was a citizen at the birth: a citizen by registration, at any age, not at birth; applying after 18, only after 3 of the 5 years before in Fiji (s. 8).
